Research experiment · 13 September 2026 · GPL source retained

Why one-hour orbital elements are unstable

Independent truth, controlled solver variants, and numerical sensitivity analysis for find-orb-wasm. The evidence separates forward propagation accuracy from the much harder problem of inferring an orbit from a short optical arc.

Decision: retain the v0.2.0 solver default. Alternative representatives have mixed outcomes. The strongest practical improvement comes from additional nights of astrometry. A source-level early return also explains why more ranging trials can produce worse results; deterministic, guarded refinement is the next algorithm experiment.

What the study established

The main errors are in orbit recovery, not forward propagation. Native and released WASM produce identical printed sky predictions in all seven independent-state controls. Across development fit comparisons, the maximum native/WASM sky difference is 4.98 × 10−8 arcseconds. The three default-instrumentation checks preserve printed WASM elements and sky exactly. Twelve further held-out released-WASM fits also agree with their native counterparts within the recorded primary tolerances.

The nominal is a heuristic representative. Upstream selects an accepted state near three coordinate-wise position medians, then takes that candidate’s velocity. The accepted set uses weighted residuals plus eccentricity, inclination, and an empirical main-belt reward. It is not a posterior sample. A trial-count change can change radial velocity and orbital energy despite nearly unchanged residuals. In the user’s FCS5000 sensitivity fixture, initial capacities 25–2,000 produce semimajor axes from 3.29 to 9.10 AU while RMS stays about 0.024″; this fixture has no independent truth and establishes sensitivity only. Seven sensitivity probes with raw commands/results. Pinned scoring and selection source.

More search can also change the algorithm. Once more than ten candidates pass the score gate, initial orbit determination returns an SR family. Existing SR sigmas ordinarily suppress later differential correction. With three-night Pallas and Vesta cases, 100 trials often reach a covariance fit, whereas 500 trials return a less accurate ranging representative. The archive retains actual attempt counts and retries; MAX_SR_ORBITS is an initial batch capacity, not always total work. Early return, refinement gate.

A native build defect was fixed. A source patch made within the same timestamp second could leave macOS make reusing the original object. The comparator build now forces recompilation with -B. Stale smoke runs were rejected; every archived experimental SR run must emit candidate and batch evidence. Production solver patches, floating-point policy, and released artifacts were not changed.

Design and scope

Eight known objects and two dates were declared before solver comparisons, with an object-level development/held-out split. The original fixed-time corpus exposed below-horizon input rejection. A separately recorded rule then selected the earliest qualifying one-hour interval: altitude at least 20°, astronomical night, a 30-day search followed by a fixed 90-day search. Seven arcs from six objects qualify; nine object/date pairs remain explicitly unavailable. Apophis and Bennu are absent from the observable set.

SplitObjects and usable arcs
DevelopmentCeres September; Pallas September; Eros March
Held outJuno March and September; Vesta September; Achilles March

Each one-hour fit uses four positions at 0, 20, 40, and 60 minutes. Horizons astrometric ICRF coordinates are reception-time UTC; heliocentric J2000 ecliptic states/elements use matched TDB/TT instants. Predictions are checked at +6 hours, +1 day, +3 days, and +7 days. A two-step propagation preserves the common element epoch for the predictive representative because the CLI’s supplied-vector path fixes its own element epoch. Horizons manual, API conventions.

The primary noise model is independent Gaussian east/north error with σ = 0.2″, using three deterministic paired realizations. Additional arms use exact coordinates, common tracklet bias σ = 0.3″, and a 3″ outlier in the third fitted position. The solver is told σ = 0.2″ in every arm. Exact input still has MPC quantization and independent force-model differences. Shared bias and the outlier deliberately violate the solver’s stated independent-error model. Nightly correlations and astrometric weighting affect uncertainty interpretation. Vereš et al., 2017.

This is an initial controlled mechanics study, not a survey-population validation: only one observable NEA, no high-eccentricity comet or interstellar case, no weather/brightness selection, and only three held-out objects. Repeated noise seeds and Juno’s two epochs are not independent objects. No population significance or broad accuracy guarantee is claimed.

Changing the representative: mixed results

MethodDefinition
Existing positionUnchanged upstream nearest coordinate-median position; actual accepted candidate.
Position + velocityNearest six coordinate medians after scaling each coordinate by its median absolute deviation. Frame dependent; not a calibrated prior.
Minimum residualAccepted candidate with the smallest weighted residual RMS. A diagnostic, not an endorsed estimator.
One-day predictiveActual candidate closest to the unweighted family mean unit direction at +1 day. Added after development results; horizon/loss frozen before held-out evaluation.

All methods retain the same acceptance rule. The predictive method’s uniform discrete measure is still the original heuristic family. Lower residuals or an estimator optimal under that measure do not imply better accuracy against nature.

A pooled median can hide regressions. At 100 trials, the position-plus-velocity median improves from 192.6″ to 138.3″, but only five of twelve paired cases improve; six worsen and one ties. Its median paired error ratio is 1.023. At 500, eight improve, three worsen, and one ties. Development cases show substantially worse orbital-energy errors and some large forecast regressions. This evidence supports further study, not default promotion.

What the mathematics explains—and what remains unproved

At each independent truth state, central finite differences form a whitened astrometric Jacobian. Position coordinates are scaled by 1 AU, velocity coordinates by 0.01720209895 AU/day, and angular residuals by 0.2″. SVD is applied directly to the Jacobian at two step sizes. All seven one-hour arcs have four numerically resolved modes and two very weak modes. The weak two-dimensional subspace is stable across steps: its principal cosines exceed 0.99999999992. Its position components align with the astrometric line of sight; a pure radial-velocity direction projects almost completely into it.

The weakest one-hour singular values are too close to the numerical diagnostic’s resolution floor to justify precise condition numbers. They are deliberately withheld. Adding one next-night position resolves all six modes under the empirical rule in five cases.

This is consistent with the attributable description: angular position and angular motion are much better constrained than range and range rate. Published systematic ranging fixes the weak variables and fits the other four. A probability model requires an explicit prior and the appropriate integration measure; logarithmic sampling adds a coordinate Jacobian. Farnocchia, Chesley & Micheli, 2015, Del Vigna, 2020.

H = ∂[(Δα cos δ)/σ, Δδ/σ] / ∂(scaled state)
H = U Σ Vᵀ
meanⱼ ‖uᵢ − uⱼ‖² = ‖uᵢ − meanⱼ uⱼ‖² + constant

The last identity explains the predictive selector’s stated real-arithmetic objective. It does not turn the candidate frequencies into posterior mass. Likewise, the empirical energy score uses unit sky vectors and includes both truth distance and ensemble spread; it evaluates the discrete predictive measure actually supplied. Gneiting & Raftery, 2007.

No full solver or compiler proof is claimed. The Jacobian is a local linearization at truth, not a deployable gate evaluated at an estimate or a proof of global uniqueness. Two finite-difference steps and output-rounding bounds do not certify total derivative error. Disconnected admissible modes can survive a good local fit, and astrometric errors can create spurious curvature. Spoto et al., 2018. Existing bounded verification remains documented in the correctness report.

Additional nights: the strongest demonstrated benefit

A single feasible next-night point improves seven-day predictions in 16/21 paired Gaussian cases at initial capacity 100; median paired improvement is 2.15×. Four objects also permit fixed four-exposure tracklets on the second and third nights. Other schedules remain explicitly unavailable rather than being adjusted after results. The original +3-day and +7-day truth positions are never fitted.

Inspect individual outcomes

Select an arc, noise model, and initial batch capacity. These rows expose regressions hidden by pooled statistics. Semimajor axis becomes ill-conditioned near a parabola; reciprocal-a error is the primary energy metric.

The next algorithm experiment

The most concrete candidate is deterministic refinement after an accepted SR family, guarded by fit quality, conditioning, and fallback to the original family. Today -j forces correction, but it retains a clock-dependent prefix of up to four calls within 250 ms. -yN adds fixed calls after that prefix; it does not solve reproducibility. A separate experiment should set explicit iteration limits, record observation rejection, and preserve a rollback candidate. CLI switches, timed refinement loop.

A usable conditioning check should operate on the solver’s full-precision residual Jacobian at estimated states, with declared scales and direct SVD, rather than rounded ephemerides or normal-equation eigenvalues. Even then, competing admissible modes must remain visible. A future systematic-ranging distribution should explicitly define its prior, grid cell measure, and any Jacobian or marginalization factor. Reweighting the current heuristic samples and calling them a calibrated posterior would be unjustified.

Expand validation before promoting either change: substantially more independent objects and geometries, nearby/high-range-rate targets, high-eccentricity and retrograde objects, timing errors, correlated catalog errors, realistic discovery selection, and withheld follow-up. The separate endpoint-range parameterization mismatch found in source remains unpatched: its tested one-hour effect was small and no lost true solution was demonstrated.

Reproducibility, checks, and provenance

The archive contains 796 planned fit comparisons/interventions, 68 numerical-control records, and 175 truth/perturbation records: 1,039 raw records total. Unavailable commands, rejected fits, strict comparison failures, raw CLI files, actual attempt counts, and exact calculation sources are retained. The seven FCS5000 sensitivity probes are a separate linked evidence file. Some predictive fit records contain additional transfer and propagation commands; record counts are not CPU-call counts.

Checks: the existing 23-test suite and all 28 research tests pass, with no skips in the recorded run. The research tests compile actual patched selector/sorting functions under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, including failure paths, family membership, default delegation, and actual loop accounting. Additional tests check spherical noise, time/angle wrapping, osculating invariants, paired inputs, empirical scoring, and the predictive-selection identity. Offline replay independently rebuilds all 796 fit records from stored commands and outputs, reproducing scientific summaries exactly: 728 valid fits, 32 invalid completed fits, and 36 unavailable commands. This checks postprocessing reproducibility, not a fresh solver execution. SVD reconstruction error is below 10⁻¹⁵. Native/WASM core fit comparisons pass; four stricter all-number checks are retained as failures solely for derived period P (0.000104–0.000391 day, relative 1.39–3.76 × 10⁻¹⁰) in nearly parabolic min-RMS solutions. Recorded checks.

Runtime numbers are diagnostic only: correctness work ran concurrently. This study does not establish a performance speedup. All empirical intervals remain uncalibrated.
